title: Radcliffe Award Border Demarcation Implementation
subtitle: Sir Cyril Radcliffe dated the Bengal Boundary Commission award 12 August 1947; it was publicly announced on 17 August, after India and Pakistan became independent
summary: Sir Cyril Radcliffe dated the Bengal Boundary Commission award 12 August 1947; it was publicly announced on 17 August, after India and Pakistan became independent. It assigned districts and subdistricts between India and Pakistan’s new province of East Bengal. Later interpretation disputes required inter-dominion arbitration.

claimCitations.claim: Sir Cyril Radcliffe dated the Bengal Boundary Commission award 12 August 1947; it was publicly announced on 17 August, after India and Pakistan became independent. It assigned districts and subdistricts between India and Pakistan’s new province of East Bengal. Later interpretation disputes required inter-dominion arbitration.

The award made partition plans a boundary affecting citizenship, migration and administration. Communal displacement and violence belong to the wider partition context and should not be attributed to a single boundary decision alone.
The award boundary became the India–East Pakistan frontier and, after 1971, the India–Bangladesh frontier; disputes over interpretation continued after partition.
